\section*{Multiple Choice (14 marks)}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\arabic*.]
\item \duallayerbox{Statement 1| The Stanford Sentiment Treebank contained movie reviews, not book reviews. Statement 2| The Penn Treebank has been used for language modeling.}{Statement 1| The Caltech-101 dataset contains object category images, not movie reviews. Statement 2| The Stanford Sentiment Treebank has not been used for language modeling.}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item True, True
    \item False, False
    \item True, False
    \item False, True
\end{enumerate}
\item Suppose your model is overfitting. \duallayerbox{Which of the following is NOT a valid way to try and reduce the overfitting?}{Which of the following is a valid way to try and reduce the overfitting?}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item Increase the amount of training data.
    \item Improve the optimisation algorithm being used for error minimisation.
    \item Decrease the model complexity.
    \item Reduce the noise in the training data.
\end{enumerate}
\item Which of the following is \duallayerbox{the joint probability of H, U, P, and W described by the given Bayesian Network H -> U <- P <- W}{a factorization that assumes all four variables H, U, P, and W are mutually independent}? [note: as the product of the...
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item P(H, U, P, W) = P(H) * P(W) * P(P) * P(U)
    \item P(H, U, P, W) = P(H) * P(W) * P(P | W) * P(W | H, P)
    \item P(H, U, P, W) = P(H) * P(W) * P(P | W) * P(U | H, P)
    \item None of the above
\end{enumerate}
\item A and B are two events. \duallayerbox{If P(A, B) decreases while P(A) increases}{If P(A, B) decreases while P(B) increases}, which of the following is true?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item P(A|B) decreases
    \item P(B|A) decreases
    \item P(B) decreases
    \item All of above
\end{enumerate}
\item What is the rank of the following matrix? \duallayerbox{A = [[1, 1, 1], [1, 1, 1], [1, 1, 1]]}{A = [[0, 0, 0], [0, 0, 0], [0, 0, 0]]}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item 0
    \item 1
    \item 2
    \item 3
\end{enumerate}
\item \duallayerbox{Statement 1| RELUs are not monotonic, but sigmoids are monotonic. Statement 2| Neural networks trained with gradient descent with high probability converge...}{Statement 1| RELUs are monotonic, and sigmoids are monotonic. Statement 2| Neural networks trained with gradient descent with high probability fail to converge to global minima.}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item True, True
    \item False, False
    \item True, False
    \item False, True
\end{enumerate}
\item Which one of the following is equal to P(A, B, C) given Boolean random variables A, B and C, and \duallayerbox{no independence or conditional independence assumptions}{the assumption that A, B and C are mutually independent}...
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item P(A | B) * P(B | C) * P(C | A)
    \item P(C | A, B) * P(A) * P(B)
    \item P(A, B | C) * P(C)
    \item P(A | B, C) * P(B | A, C) * P(C | A, B)
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}

\item True or False: \duallayerbox{The correct answer to 'Suppose we like to calculate P(H|E, F) and we have no conditional independence information. Which of the following sets of numbers are...' is 'P(E, F), P(H), P(E, F|H)'.}{The capital of Russia is Moscow.}
